answer: Batch processing is a method of ingesting data in large chunks, typically on a predetermined time interval or when a preset size threshold is reached [Ch. 2]. It is often used for analytics and machine learning [Ch. 2]. Batch ingestion involves processing data in bulk, either based on time intervals or the size of accumulated data [Ch. 7]. This approach is common in traditional business ETL for data warehousing, where data is processed once a day, overnight during off-hours, to provide daily reporting [Ch. 7]. While streaming systems are becoming more prevalent, batch processing remains a popular choice for downstream data consumption [Ch. 2].

citations.quote: Batch data is ingested either on a predetermined time interval or as data reaches a preset size threshold.
Batch processing remains an extremely popular way to ingest data for downstream consumption, particularly in analytics and ML.
This means that data is ingested by taking a subset of data from a source system, based either on a time interval or the size of accumulated data (Figure 7-10).
